newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - BAA cuts stake in Australian bid.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - BAA cuts stake in Australian bid.

text.p: UK airport group BAA Plc said on Monday it had decided to cut the stake in its bid group for Australian airports to 29 percent from 49 percent.

Russel Walls, group finance director, told Reuters "We are cutting our stake in agreement with our other partners. The bid had too high a foreign content," he said. But Walls denied there was any prompt from the Australian government to reduce its dominance in the consortium, which includes Australian fund managers.

Bids have been put in for airports in Melbourne, Brisbane and Perth. BAA already runs the UK's biggest airports and has sharply increased profitability by boosting the amount of revenues raised through shopping malls inside airports.
This was reflected in BAA's nine-month results released earlier, showing a 6.2 percent rise in pretax profits to 397 million stg for the period to December 31.

Total revenues were up 7.8 percent to 1.06 billion stg, with 76.6 million passengers travelling through BAA aiports, a rise of 4.4 percent. Walls welcomed the results and said passenger growth had seen a steady improvement since the first quarter.
